newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to start importing modified soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Germany to start importing modified soybeans.

text.p: One of Europe's largest soybean processors, Oelmuehle Hamburg AG, said on Tuesday it would begin importing and processing genetically modified soybeans from the U.S. this autumn, despite a protest campaign by environmentalist group Greenpeace.
Oelmuehle said the genetically altered soybeans would comprise only one to two percent of its imports, but for practical reasons it could not separate them.
There was no reason to do so, said chairman Arnd von Wissel, according to a statement distributed by Verband Deutscher Oelmuehlen E.V., a national lobby group.
"Products made from genetically modified soybeans are indistinguishable from conventional products," he said.

Greenpeace spokesman Joerg Naumann said his organisation wants Oelmuehle to offer products free of modified soybeans and let consumers decide. "It would be possible to store and market the types separately," Naumann said.
Earlier this month, Greenpeace said it would organise consumer protests against imports of genetically modified U.S. soybeans because risks to human health and the environment could not be ruled out.
Von Wissel said health and environmental authorities in the U.S. and the European Union have found no problems with the modified soybeans.
Oelmuehle Hamburg imported two million tonnes of soybeans in 1995 out of total German imports of 15 million tonnes.
U.S. soybeans accounted for 60 percent of its imports.
